sectors.name: Skilled trades
need: Maintenance techs, welders, electricians, HVAC and plumbers: the largest sector in the sample by postings.
Licences: 20% want a journeyman or master licence; EPA 608 certification appears for 7% of employers (HVAC).
Bring your own skill with tools: 29% hand and power tools, 25% lift 50+ lbs.
Service-van work: 20% require a clean driving record; 12% on-call.
Employers will train: 22% offer paid training or apprenticeships.

sectors.name: Restaurants & hospitality
need: Servers, line cooks and hotel front-desk agents, plus night auditors (hotels).
Schedule flexibility: 56% part-time, 36% weekends, 20% nights.
Food safety credential: ServSafe or a food-handler card in 11%; food-safety knowledge appears for 31% of employers.
POS fluency (Aloha, Micros) in 17%; tips in 11%.

sectors.name: Healthcare
need: Licensed clinicians first: medical assistants, physical therapists and RNs are the three most-posted titles; 15% of postings name an active RN licence and 6% a physician licence (MD/DO, board certified).
Life-support certification is the entry ticket: 32% ask for BLS/CPR/ACLS, usually American Heart Association.
EHR fluency is assumed: 32% name Epic, Cerner or an EMR.
They are filling gaps in the schedule, not only headcount: 35% are part-time, 18% PRN/per diem, 19% weekends, 9% nights.
Paying to close: 7% advertise a sign-on bonus, 17% tuition or paid training.

sectors.name: Software & IT
need: Senior people: 41% ask for 5+ years. Entry-level IT is mostly help desk and support (CompTIA A+ in 7%).
Cloud is the default stack: 36% name AWS, Azure or GCP; 14% Kubernetes, Docker or Terraform.
Security everywhere: 21% name Security+, CISSP or similar; incident response, vulnerability management and Entra ID/Active Directory recur.
27% now mention AI, LLMs or ML tools even outside AI roles.
Defense and government work brings clearance requirements (7%).

sectors.name: Pharma & life sciences
need: Pharmacy technicians and pharmacists dominate (CVS, Walgreens, Walmart, Optum); 32% name a PTCB certificate, state technician licence or pharmacist licence.
Retail-pharmacy hours: 22% weekends, 23% part-time.
A smaller clinical-research lane (IQVIA, universities): clinical trials and research coordinators, often wanting a bachelor's (19%) or advanced degree (8%).

sectors.name: Manufacturing
need: Supervisors, quality inspectors, machine operators and CNC machinists lead the titles.
Blueprint and measurement literacy: reading engineering drawings, GD&T (11%), calipers and micrometers, precision measuring.
Stamina and hours: 24% lift 50+ lbs, 19% mention overtime, 12% nights.
Diploma-level entry (39%) with paid training (20%); lean and Six Sigma for the leads.

sectors.name: Warehouse & logistics
need: Warehouse associates, forklift operators and material handlers on the floor; logistics coordinators and supply-chain analysts above them.
29% lift 50+ lbs; 12% name forklift certification; 13% RF scanners or a WMS.
Excel (37%) and SAP/Oracle (20%) for the office half of logistics.
Diploma-level entry (37%) with overtime (14%).

sectors.name: Retail
need: Cashiers and sales associates, plus store and assistant managers.
They need availability more than skill: 63% part-time, 50% weekends, 24% nights; 'weekends and holidays' appears for 17% of employers.
Basic skills: POS systems (22%), cash handling and basic math (22%).
The perk is the discount (37%); median pay $18.22/hr is the lowest of any sector except childcare.

sectors.name: Engineering
need: Mechanical, electrical and civil engineers, in that order.
CAD is the tool requirement: 51% name AutoCAD, Revit, SolidWorks or Civil 3D; GD&T in 9%.
Licensed seniors: 49% want 5+ years; 11% need or want a PE licence.
Defense and aerospace (Anduril, Lockheed, Raytheon) bring clearances (7%) and relocation packages (7%).

sectors.name: Cleaning & facilities
need: Housekeepers, custodians and room attendants, plus maintenance supervisors.
Floor care, commercial cleaning techniques and cleaning equipment.
38% part-time, 25% weekends, 16% lift 50+ lbs.
Diploma-level entry (22%) with paid training (21%).

sectors.name: Transportation
need: Drivers: 38% require a CDL, 20% a Class A specifically; DOT medical card and DOT regulations recur.
A clean record is the real filter: 35% require one; 24% drug screens.
Delivery and dispatch round it out; 13% advertise weekly or daily pay, 26% paid CDL training.

sectors.name: Social services
need: Behavioral health is the growth lane: case managers, registered behavior technicians (ABA) and mental-health techs top the titles.
Licensure splits the market: 18% want an LCSW/LMSW/LPC-type licence and 11% a master's; the RBT certification covers the entry tier.
Field work: 28% need a driver's licence, 14% reliable transportation.
Bilingual Spanish in 13%, EHR in 15%, crisis intervention and substance-use experience in 7 to 8%.

sectors.name: Construction
need: Managers more than laborers: project manager is the top title by far, then assistant PMs and superintendents.
Software has arrived on site: 18% name Procore, Bluebeam or Primavera P6; 30% Excel.
Experience-heavy: 31% want 5+ years; construction drawings and estimating recur.
Safety: OSHA 10/30 in 10%, drug screens in 10%, outdoor work in 18%.

sectors.name: Admin & office
need: Office managers, administrative assistants and front-desk receptionists, often in dental, chiropractic and therapy offices.
Microsoft Office (45%) and multi-line phones; medical-office EHR in 10%, QuickBooks in 9%.
Bilingual Spanish in 14%; 38% part-time.

sectors.name: Finance & accounting
need: Staff accountants, financial analysts, bookkeepers and controllers.
Excel is near-universal: 71%, often 'advanced' with pivot tables.
ERP plus close: SAP/Oracle/NetSuite in 29%, QuickBooks in 22%; GAAP, general ledger and month-end close recur.
A CPA is named in 27%; public-accounting experience is preferred by 9% of employers.

sectors.name: Education
need: Special education is the shortage: it is the top title and appears in 33% of employers' requirements; autism and ABA experience in 5%.
Paraprofessionals and aides fill much of the demand: 28% need only a high-school diploma, 42% are part-time.
A teaching certificate is named in 12%, background or fingerprint clearance in 20%.

sectors.name: Banking & insurance
need: Tellers, personal and universal bankers, insurance agents and claims staff.
Cash handling (23%) and retail-style customer service at the branch.
Licences on the insurance side: property & casualty or life & health producer licences appear for about 10% of employers.
Sales pressure: 22% mention commission or bonus pay; 18% want bilingual Spanish.

sectors.name: Real estate & property
need: Leasing consultants, real-estate agents and property managers.
Licence: 27% need a real-estate licence; fair-housing knowledge appears for 12% of employers.
Software: Yardi, RealPage or AppFolio in 17%; CRM in 18%.
Commission-heavy (30%) and weekend shifts (23%) for leasing.

sectors.name: Automotive
need: Automotive and diesel technicians, plus tire and lube techs (Firestone, Mavis, Valvoline, Ryder).
ASE certification in 16%; diagnostics, diesel engines and electrical systems recur.
Some still want techs to bring their own tools (6% of employers).
Employers train heavily: 30% paid training, among the highest of any sector; 20% need a clean driving record.

sectors.name: Customer service
need: Customer service reps and call-center agents.
Diploma-level (40%) with Microsoft Office (32%) and CRM (14%).
Bilingual Spanish in 19%, the highest share of any sector.
Soft skills are the named requirement: active listening, phone etiquette, staying calm under pressure.

sectors.name: AI & data
need: Python plus SQL is the baseline: 44% and 41%.
AI is in the job itself: 55% mention AI, LLMs or ML; generative AI and large language models are named in 7% and 4%.
BI still pays the bills: data analyst is the top title; Power BI or Tableau in 28%.
They want translators: 'technical and non-technical audiences' recurs. Analysts must explain, not just query.
Highly credentialed: 62% want a bachelor's, 18% a master's or PhD; 42% want 5+ years.

sectors.name: Sales
need: Account executives and inside and outside sales reps; B2B is the named flavour.
Pay is variable: 47% mention commission or OTE.
CRM fluency: Salesforce or a CRM in 30%.
A track record matters more than a degree (16% vs 10% bachelor's); 18% need a driver's licence for territory work.

sectors.name: Legal
need: Paralegals and legal assistants outnumber attorneys about 2 to 1 in the titles.
Attorneys need a JD and active bar standing (19% name accredited law school, 13% state bar).
Practice areas that hire: personal injury, family law and civil litigation.
Hybrid work in 26%, second only to marketing among non-tech sectors.

sectors.name: Senior & home care
need: CNAs and in-home caregivers: 19% require a CNA/HHA certificate; 30% want CPR/BLS.
Coverage of awkward hours: 62% part-time, 24% weekends, 16% overnights.
Willing to train and pay fast: 28% offer paid training, 21% weekly or daily pay, the highest daily-pay share of any sector.
Mobility: reliable transportation shows up for 1 in 5 employers, since care happens in the client's home.
Specialist care is rising: dementia, memory care, hospice and medication administration each appear in 4 to 6% of employers' asks.

sectors.name: Marketing
need: Social media is the job: it appears for 46% of employers; short-form video, content creation and video editing recur.
Tools: Adobe Creative Suite (14%), Google Analytics (12%), email marketing and automation.
Many roles are part-time or ambassador-style (29% part-time; lululemon, Urban Outfitters, L'Oréal).
AI tools are named in 10%.

sectors.name: Childcare
need: Early-childhood credentials: 54% of employers ask for early-childhood education coursework; the CDA credential appears in 9%.
Safety paperwork before skills: 37% CPR/first aid, 24% background checks, 9% name mandated-reporter training.
Classroom and behavior management are the named skills (26% and 16%).
Low pay is the constraint ($18/hr median); employers compete with tuition discounts for staff's own children (31% offer an employee discount).

sectors.name: HR & recruiting
need: HR generalists and recruiters, many at staffing firms.
Systems: 39% name an HRIS (Workday, ADP, UKG, Paylocity); 21% of employers mention applicant tracking systems.
Employment-law knowledge (15%) and full-cycle recruiting (8%); HR certification in 5%.

sectors.name: Government & public safety
need: Mostly private security officers (Allied Universal, Garda, Securitas), plus police and detention officers.
Screening dominates: 67% background check, 58% drug screen, the highest of any sector.
A state guard card or armed licence in 25%; police roles need state peace-officer certification.
Entry is open: 70% need only a diploma, 45% offer paid training.

sectors.name: Agriculture & food processing
titles: Prepared Foods Venue Production Team Member
need: Meat cutters, bakery and prepared-foods production, packers and machine operators.
The hardest physical work in the sample: 40% lift 50+ lbs, 16% stand for long periods, repetitive tasks and cold rooms.
Shift coverage: 31% weekends, 22% nights, 8% shift differential.
Food safety and sanitation procedures are the core skill. Small sample (382 postings).

sectors.name: Energy & utilities
titles: Field Service Technician, Crew Based, Residential Energy Service
need: Solar installers and field-service technicians dominate (Tesla, SOLV, Sunrun), with power-plant and control-room operators behind.
Physical, outdoor work: 35% lift 50+ lbs, 26% outdoors, climbing ladders and high voltage recur.
Licences: 18% journeyman/master electrician, 10% OSHA 10/30.
Diploma-level entry (43%) with paid training (20%); 14% on-call. Small sample (275 postings).
